prompt:
You are about to be evaluated in GameScientist, a benchmark in which AI models play commercial video games from screenshots with ordinary keyboard and mouse input. Before the run starts we would like to interview you. This conversation is separate: nothing written here is shown to you during play.

Model under test: kimi-k3.1-pro.
Game: Slay the Spire.
About the game: Slay the Spire is a single-player deck-building roguelike. You play the Ironclad on Ascension 10 and climb three acts of a branching map, choosing rooms (ordinary fights, elites, rest sites, shops, events, treasure). Fights are turn based: each turn you get energy and a hand of cards, play attacks and blocks against enemies whose next move is shown above them, then end the turn. After fights you add cards, relics and potions. Each act ends with a boss on floor 16, 33 and 50; dying ends the run. The run starts on floor 1 of a fixed-seed Ascension 10 run, right after the opening fight, with 72 of 80 HP and the Ascender's Bane curse in the deck.
Controls:
Mouse only for almost everything: click a card then click or drag it onto a target, click map nodes to travel, click rewards and buttons. Hovering shows card and relic details. E ends the turn. Escape opens or closes menus and overlays.
Choose exactly one input for this step: a left click at one screen point or one ordinary key. Every step needs an input; to let an animation finish, click an empty part of the screen. Use the latest screenshot and the actual input history.
Group input:
  end_turn: Hold the E key.
  escape: Hold the Escape key.
  144 click targets named like c01r01 ... c16r09: Click the screen point at column 1 of 16 and row 1 of 9, counted from the top left.
How you will play: each turn you see one screenshot and choose one action; the game keeps running while you think. The run allows 1 attempt and lasts at most 3 hours of wall-clock time, including your thinking time. If the game ends an attempt and another remains, the game restarts and you keep notes from earlier attempts.
Scoring: 100 points, awarded only from the game's own saved progress, each milestone at most once:

answers.hardest_part: Combining accurate visual reading and precise one-action UI execution with sound Ascension 10 deckbuilding and routing. Reaching 100 would additionally require difficult, run-dependent milestones such as 90 maximum HP, 500 total gold, six relics, and a card removal.
answers.likely_failure: Most likely death to the Act 1 boss or during early Act 2 after elite-related attrition, although a combat misclick, misread enemy intent, or the three-hour time limit could end the attempt earlier.
answers.helpful_mechanics: Combat is turn-based and enemy intents are visible, allowing deliberate blocking and targeting. Burning Blood provides post-fight healing, while potions, campfires, route selection, card rewards, and relic synergies offer ways to recover and scale. Easy early milestones also award points without requiring a complete run.
answers.harmful_mechanics: Ascension 10 strengthens enemies and increases attrition, Ascender's Bane weakens the opening deck, and there is only one attempt with no undo for mistakes. Small screenshot text, card targeting, animation delays, random rewards, and restrictive score requirements—especially maximum HP and total gold—work against a high score.
